content.text:
The pattern is a single phase: **mp-1272748 (Sr2VMoO6)**. Its simulated pattern matches every observed reflection in both position and relative intensity.

| Observed peak (2θ, degrees) | Observed intensity | Sr2VMoO6 simulated intensity |
|---|---|---|
| 15.6 | ~9 | ~6 |
| 28.0 | ~6 | ~3.6 |
| 32.1–32.5 (main peak, with shoulder) | 100 | 100 |
| 39.3 | ~11 | ~9.5 |
| 45.6 / 46.3 doublet | ~19 / ~30 | ~17 / ~30 |
| 57.4 / 58.0 doublet | ~17 / ~35 | ~18 / ~33 |
| 67.7 / 68.2 doublet | ~18 / ~10 | ~18 / ~9 |
| 75.7 / 76.6 doublet | ~8 / ~11 | ~7 / ~11 |

I also simulated the two other perovskite-like candidates, and neither fits:
- **mp-22391 (Sr3V2O7)** has a single, narrower main peak near 32.3°. It lacks the 15.6° and 39.3° peaks and doesn't reproduce the doublet intensity ratios.
- **mp-1293586 (BaYMnCoO5)** puts its main peak lower, around 31.5–32.0°. It predicts a peak near 11.3° that isn't observed and has a different split pattern above 55°.

Nothing in the observed pattern is left unexplained, so there's no evidence of a second phase. I didn't simulate the remaining six candidates.

{"present": ["mp-1272748"], "confidence": 0.95, "note": "The simulated Sr2VMoO6 pattern matches all observed peaks, including the split doublets at 45.6/46.3, 57.4/58.0, 67.7/68.2 and 75.7/76.6 degrees, with no peaks left unexplained."}
